precepts.text: Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God; that is the offering of him that has no gold nor silver.
precepts.point: The badgers' skins settle a confusion: the Lord commanded Israel to handle animal skins and hair to build his own tabernacle. So the laws about not touching that which is defiled, the carcass of the unclean beast, go into the matter of sacrifice and coming into the temple, not into everyday handling. A boar-bristle brush is not sin; brush your hair, brothers.

note.label: Exodus 25: The Pattern of the Tabernacle

precepts.why:
The offering for the tabernacle was “gold, and silver, and brass, And blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats’ hair, And rams’ skins dyed red, and badgers’ skins, and shittim wood, Oil for the light, spices for anointing oil, and for sweet incense, Onyx stones, and stones to be set in the ephod, and in the breastplate.” Thank the Most High he requires no gold and silver now, for half of us would have nothing to give. Under the new covenant the offering is this: “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” The body presented a living sacrifice is the offering of him that has no gold nor silver.

The badgers’ skins in this offering settle a confusion. The Lord commanded Israel to handle animal skins and hair to build his own tabernacle. So the laws about not touching that which is defiled, the carcass of the unclean beast, go into the matter of sacrifice and coming into the temple, not into everyday handling. A boar-bristle brush is not sin. Brush your hair, brothers.

precepts.text: There I will meet with thee, and I will commune with thee from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims.
precepts.point: When Moses was gone into the tabernacle of the congregation to speak with him, that is Moses going in to speak with the Most High. The voice came from off the mercy seat that was upon the ark of testimony, from between the two cherubims, exactly where the Lord said he would meet and commune with him.

note.label: Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar

precepts.why:
When Moses went into the tabernacle of the congregation to speak with him, that is Moses going in to speak with the Most High. He heard the voice “from off the mercy seat that was upon the ark of testimony, from between the two cherubims”, exactly where the Lord said he would meet him.

“And thou shalt put the mercy seat above upon the ark; and in the ark thou shalt put the testimony that I shall give thee. And there I will meet with thee, and I will commune with thee from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims which are upon the ark of the testimony, of all things which I will give thee in commandment unto the children of Israel.”

What the Lord promised at Sinai, that he would meet and commune with Moses from above the mercy seat, is what happened in the tabernacle after the altar was dedicated.

precepts.text: The staves are set in the rings so the ark is borne, and the staves are not to be taken out.
precepts.point: The Levites bore the ark upon their shoulders with the staves, as Moses commanded according to the word of the Most High.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 15: None Ought to Carry the Ark but the Levites

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt put the staves into the rings by the sides of the ark, that the ark may be borne with them. The staves shall be in the rings of the ark: they shall not be taken from it.” The staves are set in the rings so the ark is borne, and they are not to be taken out.

The first attempt failed, “for that we sought him not after the due order.” This time “the children of the Levites bare the ark of God upon their shoulders with the staves thereon, as Moses commanded according to the word of the Lord.” The due order is the order Moses was given.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

precepts.why: “I am the light of the world”: the Israelite world. “He that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.” The light of the lamps in the tabernacle was Christ. Christ is our tabernacle.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

precepts.why: Still explaining the light in the tabernacle: even the menorah was only a representation of Christ. “There will I make the horn of David to bud”, just as Aaron’s rod budded. “I have ordained a lamp for mine anointed.” The horn of David is Christ; he is the anointed, and he is that light.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

precepts.why: “For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”. All of it is a representation of Jesus Christ.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

precepts.why:
Christ is that light that was in the tabernacle by way of the menorah. “Being turned, I saw seven golden candlesticks; And in the midst of the seven candlesticks one like unto the Son of man”: Christ, in the middle of the light, illuminating more than the lamps.

“His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow”: woolly textured hair, all white. “His eyes were as a flame of fire”: he drank wine, turned water into wine, and the Pharisees called him a winebibber. “His feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace”: brown; that is how you refine brass, you burn it. He was black, blacky black. “His voice as the sound of many waters”, like thunder.

The point is the candlesticks: Christ was the same illumination we saw in the tabernacle. The glory over the mercy seat, the menorah, all of it was a representation of Christ.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

precepts.why:
“The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches”: the messengers, the leaders of the seven churches, “and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches.” All a representation of Jesus Christ; the whole Bible is. Lo, I come in the volume of the book.

Remember, he sends forth his messenger to prepare his way. We are the messengers of God, all of us, the prophets: the ambassadors of Christ, laying forth the way and preparing this whole world for the entrance of Jesus Christ.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Breakdown Of Revelation 16

precepts.why: “And look that thou make them after their pattern, which was shewed thee in the mount.” When the Lord gave Moses the pattern of the candlestick, the ark of the covenant and the tabernacle, everything was based on the patterns of things in the heavens.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 4 Kingdom Vision

precepts.why:
The candlestick is the menorah, made of pure gold and beaten work, with its shaft, branches, bowls, knops and flowers of the same material. The gold was beautifully decorated. Six branches came out of the central shaft, three on either side. That makes seven with the centre, not eight as Amalek has it.

“And look that thou make them after their pattern, which was shewed thee in the mount.” Moses was shown the pattern, not merely told about it. God gave him a glimpse of the heavenly menorah and told him to make it like that. Its earthly design came from what was already in heaven.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt take fine flour, and bake twelve cakes thereof”: the cakes are the showbread, twelve loaves. “And thou shalt set them in two rows, six on a row, upon the pure table before the Lord”: the showbread table. “Even an offering made by fire unto the Lord”: the showbread is an offering made by fire; you baked the bread by fire unto the Lord.

“Every sabbath he shall set it in order before the Lord continually”: every Sabbath they baked the bread. “And it shall be Aaron’s and his sons’; and they shall eat it in the holy place”: the showbread was to be eaten by Aaron and his sons. That’s the offering.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: This confirms when the bread is baked. Other of their brethren, “of the sons of the Kohathites”, the sons of Levi, “were over the shewbread, to prepare it every sabbath.” It was hot fresh bread every Sabbath; the Levites were allowed to do this.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: “And upon the table of shewbread they shall spread a cloth of blue, and put thereon the dishes, and the spoons, and the bowls, and covers to cover withal: and the continual bread shall be thereon”: on every Sabbath. The showbread is made and baked, set six in a row, six here and six there, freshly baked every Sabbath by Aaron and his sons and their children’s children down the line.

note.label: The 4 Temples In Jerusalem

precepts.why:
Read right after the Lord told Moses to make the two cherubims: “Take ye therefore good heed unto yourselves; for ye saw no manner of similitude on the day that the Lord spake unto you in Horeb out of the midst of the fire: lest ye corrupt yourselves, and make you a graven image”, the likeness of male or female, of any beast, of any winged fowl, of any thing that creepeth, of any fish. Then: “lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them, and serve them.”

He said this in Deuteronomy 4 and in Exodus 20, and still he commanded images of angels on the ark. Nobody finds that strange, because the point was never the image: it was being driven to worship and serve it.

That is why these scriptures matter today. Certain Christians who hate black images suddenly found Deuteronomy 4 and Exodus 20 about graven images when they saw a black Christ. All the years they had the white Jesus they never saw those scriptures. That is suspicious.

note.label: The 4 Temples In Jerusalem

precepts.why:
“Take this book of the law, and put it in the side of the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, that it may be there for a witness against thee.”

Not only did the Lord give Moses the testimony of creation and the history from let there be light to the time of Moses; he was also giving Moses the law. That took time, and that is what was being done in those forty days. All that Moses wrote down was put in the side of the ark of the covenant as a witness against us.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why: The seven golden candlesticks. “And thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold: of beaten work shall the candlestick be made: his shaft, and his branches, his bowls, his knops, and his flowers, shall be of the same. And six branches shall come out of the sides of it; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side:” It is describing the menorah that was in the temple. So John saw the same thing on the island of Patmos as he stood there and turned to see the voice that was talking to him.

moments.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: Speak unto the children of Israel, that they bring me an offering: of every man that giveth it willingly with his heart ye shall take my offering. The Lord wants a willing heart in giving, not grudgingly or of necessity or only because the law says so, but because you know your giving benefits someone in need or the house of God, whatever it needs, the lights, the roof, the floor, the tables, the leadership's travel.

note.label: Exodus 25: The Pattern of the Tabernacle

points: The offering was gold, silver, brass, blue, purple, and scarlet, fine linen, goats' hair, rams' skins dyed red, badgers' skins, shittim wood, oil for the light, spices, and onyx stones for the ephod and the breastplate. Thank the Most High he requires no gold and silver now, for half of us would have nothing to give; under the new covenant the offering is the body presented a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable.

note.label: Exodus 25: The Pattern of the Tabernacle

points: The badgers' skins settle a confusion: the Lord commanded Israel to handle animal skins and hair to build his own tabernacle. So the laws about not touching that which is defiled, the carcass of the unclean beast, go into the matter of sacrifice and coming into the temple, not into everyday handling. A boar-bristle brush is not sin; brush your hair, brothers.

note.label: Exodus 25: The Pattern of the Tabernacle

points: Let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them. According to all that I shew thee, after the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all the instruments thereof, even so shall ye make it. Shew is the old English; everything was built after the pattern the Lord shewed.

note.label: Exodus 25: The Pattern of the Tabernacle

points: The ark of shittim wood: two cubits and a half the length, a cubit and a half the breadth and the height. A cubit as we know it is about eighteen inches, and it differed with the size of men in each time; when men were bigger the cubit was bigger.

note.label: Exodus 25: The Pattern of the Tabernacle

points: It was overlaid with pure gold within and without, with a crown of gold round about, four rings of gold in the corners, and staves of shittim wood overlaid with gold to bear it; the staves were not to be taken from it. And into the ark was put the testimony which the Lord gave.

note.label: Exodus 25: The Pattern of the Tabernacle

points: The mercy seat of pure gold sat above upon the ark, with two cherubims of gold of beaten work on the two ends, stretching forth their wings on high, covering the mercy seat, their faces one to another looking toward the mercy seat.

note.label: Exodus 25: The Pattern of the Tabernacle

points: There I will meet with thee, and I will commune with thee from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims which are upon the ark of the testimony, of all things which I will give thee in commandment unto the children of Israel.

note.label: Exodus 25: The Pattern of the Tabernacle

points: Understand how we lived: in our kingdom everything was overlaid with pure gold, clean and royal, with the order of kings, priests, counsellors, and the royal garments. Some nations do a good job in their films of bringing their old royal culture to remembrance for their people; that order and gold is how Israel used to live, and we are going back to it.

note.label: Exodus 25: The Pattern of the Tabernacle

points: The table of shittim wood was overlaid with pure gold, with a crown of gold round about: the crown is the molding going around the table, like the crown molding some have in their houses today. It bore the dishes, spoons, covers, and bowls, all of pure gold, and the shewbread was set upon it before the Lord alway.

note.label: Exodus 25: The Pattern of the Tabernacle

points: The candlestick of pure gold is the menorah, one beaten work: his shaft, his branches, his bowls, his knops, and his flowers of the same. Six branches come out of the sides of it, three out of the one side and three out of the other, with the shaft in the middle: seven lamps in all.

note.label: Exodus 25: The Pattern of the Tabernacle

points: A ten-candle candlestick is not the pattern given of God; the scripture gives seven, one in the middle and three coming out on each side, with bowls made like unto almonds with a knop and a flower.

note.label: Exodus 25: The Pattern of the Tabernacle

points: The seven lamps were lit that they may give light over against it: it was not small, for it had to light up a whole section of the tabernacle. The tongs and the snuffdishes were of pure gold, of a talent of pure gold, and all these vessels were made after the pattern shewed in the mount.

note.label: Exodus 25: The Pattern of the Tabernacle

points: “Thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold”, with “six branches” coming out of its sides, three on one side and three on the other: that is the menorah.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

points: “And thou shalt make the seven lamps thereof”: seven lamps. Not ten, not nine, not eight; stop following Amalek. “That they may give light over against it.” That light was used inside the tabernacle. Christ, in his presence and his glory, replaced it: he is the light we have to follow.

note.label: Christ Is Our Tabernacle

points: Rome did not give us their own calendar, and you cannot have two seventh-day sabbaths in one week. “And thou shalt set upon the table shewbread before me alway.” The showbread table is temple furniture. There’s a reason for going into the showbread.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “Thou shalt put into the ark the testimony which I shall give thee.” The Lord was going to give Moses a testimony. People think Moses was on the mountain forty days and forty nights just to get the ten commandments, but it does not take forty days to get ten commandments.

It would take that long to get the testimony from Genesis up to the time Israel was in the wilderness: the Lord explaining creation to Moses from let there be light, the first day through the seventh, the sabbath given to us, Adam and Eve put out of the garden, their children, and all that history. That is what the Lord gave Moses in those forty days.

note.label: The 4 Temples In Jerusalem

points: A mercy seat of pure gold, and “two cherubims of gold, of beaten work”, one on each end of the mercy seat. “The cherubims shall stretch forth their wings on high, covering the mercy seat with their wings, and their faces shall look one to another.” God himself commanded Moses to make two angels, with their faces toward each other and their wings stretched out, and set them on the ark of the covenant.

note.label: The 4 Temples In Jerusalem

points: “There I will meet with thee, and I will commune with thee from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims which are upon the ark of the testimony.” The Lord already gave Moses the law against graven images, and in the same breath told him to make two images of cherubims, which are angels, and put them on the ark. That was not unlawful. The key was not to bow down to them and worship them.

note.label: The 4 Temples In Jerusalem

points: “Thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold”: this is the menorah. “Six branches shall come out of the sides of it; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side.” One main candlestick, three branches on one side and three on the other: the seven-branched menorah. Not eight, not nine. The Bible tells you exactly how many it is, if you read.
